question: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left) Subject:

The European Union is confronted with immediate risks to its energy security and the unhindered functioning of critical infrastructure, as the war in the Middle East is evolving into the most significant energy crisis of recent decades1. The head of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, has warned that Europe has ‘maybe six weeks or so of jet fuel left’, highlighting the risk of imminent disruptions to aviation in the event of a prolonged disruption of energy flows2. Taking into account that the Airports Council International Europe has warned that Europe may face a systemic shortage of aviation fuel within three weeks if activity in the Strait of Hormuz is not restored, calling for urgent and coordinated action at EU level3, that the summer tourist season is approaching and that air transport – especially in countries with very high levels of tourism activity such as Greece – is expected to increase significantly, can the Commission say: 1.
Does it confirm the above, and what is its assessment of the adequacy of the aviation fuel supply and the availability of aviation fuel across the EU?

What measures does it intend to take to prevent and manage any disruptions to the functioning of the European aviation network and to safeguard the rights of air passengers in the event of flight cancellations or price increases?
What measures is it planning to ensure adequate air connectivity, in particular for island and remote areas of the EU, and for tourist destinations, in view of the summer season?

The shipping route through which around a fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas supplies passed before the war has almost come to a complete standstill since its outbreak on 28 February. According to the Financial Times, around 40 % of the global supply of aviation fuel passes through the Strait of Hormuz. https://apnews.com/video/europe-has-maybe-6-weeks-of-jet-fuel-left-energy-agency-head-tells-apd78d8b0e004d45a1b6368870dcaad2a7. https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/04/10/airport-council-warns-hormuz-closure-poses-major-fuelshortage-risks.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.6.2026) 1. As confirmed during the weekly meetings of the Oil Coordination Group with Member States and Industry representatives, while the stock level of some fuels has decreased, there is no immediate threat to the security of supply in the EU. To strengthen preparedness, and as announced in the AccelerateEU Communication1, the Commission is establishing a fuel observatory to monitor EU production, imports, exports and fuel stocks. This will improve visibility over supply and demand, help detect shortages, and support targeted action such as alternative sourcing or coordinated stock releases in the EU. 2. As announced in the AccelerateEU Communication, the Commission also issued, on 8 May 2026, guidance on the flexibilities offered by EU aviation legislation to ensure a coordinated response across Member States2. This covers airport slots3, travellers and passenger rights4, fuel uplift obligations under ReFuelEU Aviation5, Public Service Obligations (PSOs)6, and the use of alternative jet fuel sources. Specifically on passenger and traveller rights, the guidance recalls the strong protection granted under EU law, including concerning the rules on price transparency. 3. The Commission recognises the specific challenges faced by islands, where air connectivity is essential. The AccelerateEU Communication addresses the potential impact of fuel supply disruptions and sets out measures to preserve the proper functioning of the Single Market while safeguarding essential air connectivity across the EU, including island regions.
